title: Affine root scheme represents roots on all test schemes
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq1$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $P=\operatorname{Spec}(R[t]/(t^n-1))$, using polynomial rings [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and quotient algebras [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Write $x\in\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)$ for the class of $t$; it is a unit with inverse $x^{n-1}$. For every $V$-scheme $U$ [def-pc-scheme], pullback of $x$ gives a bijection
$$\operatorname{Mor}_V(U,P)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{z\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:z^n=1\},\qquad a\longmapsto a^\sharp(x),$$
natural in all morphisms of $V$-schemes $U$. In particular this identifies the representable sheaf $h_P$, $h_P(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_V(W,P)$ [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf], on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with the underlying sheaf of sets of the roots sheaf [def-asd-etale-roots-of-unity]. For every morphism of schemes $v:V'\to V$ and $P'=V'\times_VP$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projection $p:P'\to P$, the same formula $a\mapsto a^\sharp(p^\sharp x)$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Mor}_{V'}(U,P')$ to these roots for every $V'$-scheme $U$, natural in $U$. Under these bijections base-changing $a:U\to P$ sends its root to the pullback of that root along $V'\times_VU\to U$.

source.place: Tag 040M, example-roots-of-unity (including its base-change paragraph); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PK, section-kummer

proof.text: Put $B=R[t]/(t^n-1)$ and let $q$ be the quotient map. Its kernel gives $q(t)^n=1$. The identification $B=\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)$ gives $x^n=1$, hence $xx^{n-1}=x^{n-1}x=1$ since $n\geq1$. Give $P$ its structure map induced by $R\to B$.

For any $s:U\to V$ put $C=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ and $\rho=s^\sharp$. The relative affine classification gives $\operatorname{Mor}_V(U,P)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-alg}}(B,C)$. Apply the polynomial quotient equivalence to $f=t^n-1$: its forward map is $\varphi\mapsto\varphi(q(t))$, and its inverse is $q(\sum_i r_it^i)\mapsto\sum_i\rho(r_i)c^i$. Thus the composite is exactly $a\mapsto a^\sharp(x)$ and is bijective onto $\{c\in C:c^n=1\}$. Such $c$ has inverse $c^{n-1}$, and a unit is determined by its underlying element, giving the asserted bijection with roots in $C^\times$. No affineness of $U$ is used.

source.place: Tag 040M, example-roots-of-unity, algebraic and relative affine functor of points

proof.text: For $h:U_1\to U_2$ over $V$, the relative affine classification gives $(a\circ h)^\sharp(x)=h^\sharp(a^\sharp(x))$. Ring maps preserve powers, $1$, and the inverse $c^{n-1}$; hence the bijections are natural as maps to roots in units.

Restrict to the small etale site. The roots sheaf is the kernel of the power map. The sectionwise kernel comparison, including its canonical inclusion, identifies a section with its unit $z$ satisfying $z^n=1$ and commutes with restrictions. In additive notation this is $nz=0$; removing ULift and Additive changes only notation. Therefore the natural bijections of steps 2--3 identify the two presheaves, with the kernel inclusion sending the image of $a$ to $a^\sharp(x)$. Since the roots presheaf is a sheaf, the transported presheaf isomorphism is the claimed identification of sheaves.

source.place: Tag 03PK, section-kummer, first paragraph; sites-modules.tex Tag 03CO, lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves (2)

proof.text: For arbitrary $v:V\prime\to V$ use the base-change part of the relative affine classification with $Q=P$. Compose $E^v_U$ with the same polynomial quotient equivalence and the conversion from roots to units of step 2. This is a bijection with value $a^\sharp(p^\sharp x)$; its precomposition formula proves naturality. For the base change $a\prime$ of $a$, that classification gives $E^v_{U\prime}(a\prime)=r^\sharp\circ E_U(a)$. Evaluating at $q(t)$ gives $(a\prime)^\sharp(p^\sharp x)=r^\sharp(a^\sharp x)$, exactly the required compatibility. The classification allows nonaffine $V\prime$ and imposes no flatness.
